title: Rotating opaque request metadata token shim for long-lived SDK transports
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Background:
Long-lived transports (WebSocket, gRPC streams, persistent HTTP/2 connections) create a challenge for request provenance and lightweight tracing: including full header baggage on every message increases wire size and CPU work, but keeping a single static opaque provenance token across the entire connection means token compromise or TTL mismatch loses fidelity or security.

Goal:
Design and implement a minimal SDK/middleware shim that rotates an opaque request-provenance token on a configurable cadence or byte-count for long-lived transports. The token should be compact, cryptographically opaque to upstream services, and stitchable back to a trace/span so that backend telemetry (spans/metrics/logs) can correlate to originating logical requests without bloating every frame.

Key requirements:
- Zero or minimal changes for servers that do not opt into rotation: servers must accept tokens as opaque and treat them like existing provenance headers.
- Low CPU and allocation overhead in the SDK path; rotation must be amortized and nonblocking for hot paths.
- Ability to map rotated tokens to trace IDs for observability (i.e., backend should be able to map token->trace via a lookup table held in the edge or ingest pipeline).
- TTL and replay resistance: tokens should include a short-lived MAC and sequence counter to detect reuse.
- Backward compatibility: when feature disabled, behavior falls back to current single-token header.

Design overview:
1) Token format: 8-byte random nonce + 4-byte epoch counter + 8-byte truncated HMAC-SHA256 (opaque). Base64-url encoded to keep headers ASCII-safe.
2) Rotation triggers: configurable by SDK: (a) time window (default 60s), (b) bytes sent threshold (default 64KB), or (c) explicit API call from application (for bulk message bursts).
3) Client SDK behavior: maintain current token per-connection in a lock-free atomic; rotation performed on a background timer/worker that precomputes the next token and swaps it atomically to avoid blocking request send.
4) Minimal wire: add single header X-RW-ROT-TOKEN on frames/messages. The header length is ~28 bytes after encoding.
5) Server/ingest behavior: ingest accepts X-RW-ROT-TOKEN and attaches a transient mapping from token->(trace_id, request_meta) into the edge cache (LRU with TTL) so downstream collectors can join spans; if ingest doesn't find mapping, fallback to reading existing full baggage/header.
6) Security: HMAC key rotation performed by control plane and rotated into SDK secrets via KMS; SDK caches the current key and public key id.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Including full trace id in every message: simpler but costly in wire size, not acceptable for high-throughput streaming use cases.
- Symmetric vs asymmetric token signing: symmetric (HMAC) chosen for speed; asymmetric would increase token size and crypto cost.
- Server push of tokens vs client-side only rotation: push model complicates intermediaries; client-side chosen for deterministic behavior.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Feature gate in SDK with opt-in environment variable RW_ROTATING_TOKEN=true. No server changes required. Collect telemetry on header adoption and token churn.
- Phase 1: Edge proxies (ingest) enable transient token->trace mapping and populate join table. Release to limited tenants with streaming workloads.
- Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 50% of streaming traffic, with circuit-breaker that disables rotation if token miss rate or increased tail latency observed.
- Phase 3: Default enable for all SDKs after security review and stability metrics met.

Observability and testing:
- Add dashboard panels: token churn rate, token-miss rate (ingest couldn't map token->trace), avg mapping lookup latency, and 99/999 tail for request latency for streaming RPCs.
- E2E tests: simulate high-concurrency streams, validate token mapping correctness, ensure no request blocking during rotation.
- Load testing: measure allocations and latency of SDK send path with rotation enabled vs disabled.

Open questions / blockers:
- Does the edge cache add operational cost or memory pressure for high-cardinality tenants? (Ops input required)
- Confirm HMAC key distribution model across private deployments (on-prem customers may require alternate KMS flows).
- Decide default rotation cadence for low-bandwidth mobile clients vs high-throughput server-to-server streams.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes opt-in rotating token feature with time/bytes/explicit triggers
Background rotation does not add synchronous allocation on hot send path (verified by benchmark)
Edge ingest successfully maps rotated token to trace_id for >99.5% of test messages under normal conditions
Grafana panels show token churn and token-miss metrics; alert if token-miss > 0.5% over 5m
Security review completed and HMAC key lifecycle documented
notes: 2026-02-26: Spike complete. Prototype token format and local rotation worker implemented in Go SDK. Microbenchmarks show <0.6us median overhead on send path when precomputed.
2026-03-03: Design review with Security. Agreed on HMAC approach and KMS-backed key rotation. Security requested threat model doc (link added to spec).
2026-03-08: UX/Console owner (Marina Li) suggested adding token-miss metric to per-tenant cost dashboard. Added to links.
2026-03-12: Integration PR opened for Go SDK (link above). Need follow-up PRs for Node and Python SDKs. Assigned Diego for Node prototype.
